title: Managers, musicians' treatment and red beans with Louis
summary: Stella discusses managers and hard treatment of musicians, then recalls cooking red beans for Joe and Louis Armstrong whenever Louis visited.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: He'd have been popular again. Oh, yes. People would have appreciated him then again. They do now, but it's too late. Yes, yes. It's too late. It's too late. Yes, it's too late.
But, as I said, he was a grandfella to know. Grandfella to know. But he wanted to manage his own business.
Well, it would be better that way if he could have made it that way, rather than the manager takes half of their pay sometimes, too, you know.

That's what he said. But you can't make it all. No, that's right. No. Look, Louie and Louie wouldn't be in Louie Armstrong today. Yes, that's right. As if he didn't have the manager, somebody behind him. And sometimes even the men go ahead of him. Yes. See what treatment they get. Because they get an awful hard treatment. Musicians, some people don't want them in their house. Yes, that's right. And their meals, sometimes they don't have the meals and all of that. But as I can remember, so many things. And when Louie was in St. Louis, he'd come home and stop with us. And he just loved you. He idolized you. He idolized you. And Joe was crazy about him. They'd come home and I'd fix red beans for them. I know they like red beans. Well, whenever Louie would go home, I had red beans. And I'd cook a big pot and put it in a big dish and put it on the table. And we used to put the hot bones, what they call them. That was the best meat. It's near the knee bone, you know. Oh, yes. And you cook that until it's done, red beans. And you put it in the beans. That's ham, is it? Ham, yes. Ham, yes. And season up them beans and he and Louie would wash that bone. They'd wash it. Louie would wash it. Joe would wash Louie. And all of a sudden they'd make a great big jump to make us laugh. They'd have fun. They'd see who was going to get that last bone. But they were funny. To be together, they had a lot of fun together. Those two boys had a lot of fun together. And he'd come home and he'd stop. Well, when he'd stop home with me, he'd give, after Louie would come back from playing, he'd get his dress. He'd give all of us a physique. Everybody got to take physique with Louie. Everybody got to take physique.
Louie's still there, right? He's still, he's a thriss-criss.
